evidence_items.source_quote: Serologic tests for schistosomiasis, hydatidosis, distomiasis, amebiasis, toxocariasis, and trichinosis were negative, and parasites were not found in stool samples.

rationale: A 55-year-old male soldier presenting with pulmonary tuberculosis caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis subsp canetti. Serologic testing for amebiasis was explicitly negative and stool analysis showed no parasites. Amoebiasis was evaluated as part of a parasitic workup for hypereosinophilia and ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: His blood culture grew Salmonella paratyphi A. Serologies for amoeba and hydatid disease were negative.

rationale: A 74-year-old male with fever following travel to India found to have a liver abscess in a pre-existing simple liver cyst. Serology for amoeba was explicitly negative. Both blood and abscess aspirate cultures grew Salmonella paratyphi A, definitively confirming a bacterial paratyphoid abscess and excluding amoebiasis -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: A survey for infectious etiologies associated with eosinophilia revealed a negative Entamoeba histolytica, Toxocara, Trichinella, Strongyloides stercoralis, Hepatitis B and C, and HIV serologies.

rationale: A 43-year-old female presenting with idiopathic hypereosinophilia and warm autoimmune hemolytic anemia. An infectious evaluation was conducted to exclude parasitic causes of eosinophilia, and Entamoeba histolytica serology was explicitly negative. Target disease excluded -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Hepatotropic viruses, adenovirus, CMV, HIV, EBV, Coxiella burnetii, Yersinia enterocolitica, and Entamoeba histolytica were negative.

rationale: A 35-year-old female presenting with fever, diarrhea, and pulmonary infiltrates complicating eosinophilic gastroenteritis. Serologic and infectious testing for Entamoeba histolytica was explicitly negative. Target disease excluded -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Serologies for Entamoeba histolytica, Echinococcus, hepatitis, HIV, interferon gamma assay were all unrevealing.

rationale: A 46-year-old male with diabetes presenting with abdominal pain and large multiloculated liver abscess. Amoebic serology was unrevealing, and CT-guided percutaneous drainage cultures confirmed Lactobacillus gasseri bacteremia and pyogenic liver abscess. Amoebic etiology excluded -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Entamoeba Histolytica was absent in stool: consequently, no infectious disease was found, and the cause of jaundice remained unexplained.

rationale: A 55-year-old female presenting with severe hemobilia from a right hepatic artery pseudoaneurysm post-laparoscopic cholecystectomy. Stool testing confirmed Entamoeba histolytica was absent. Target disease ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Tests for amebiasis, Clostridium difficile infections, hepatitis viruses were negative, but blood cultures for Fusobacterium necrophorum were positive.

rationale: A 54-year-old female presenting with abdominal Lemierre's syndrome and superior mesenteric vein thrombosis. Diagnostic evaluation for infectious etiologies of diarrhea and fever was negative for amebiasis, while blood cultures confirmed Fusobacterium necrophorum. Amoebiasis definitively ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: The following serological studies were carried out: hepatitis A virus; Epstein-Barr virus; Trypanosoma cruzi; cytomegalovirus; Ac HBs; Ag HBs; Ac HBc T; HIV 1 + 2; Toxoplasma gondii; Entamoeba histolytica; Echinococcus granulosus; Taenia solium (IgG); Leishmania spp.; strongyloides and schistosoma. All results were negative and do not showed acute infection, except schistosoma with IgM and IgG positive.

rationale: A 45-year-old male evaluated for a retroperitoneal paraaortic mass. Comprehensive infectious serology for Entamoeba histolytica was explicitly negative. The patient was diagnosed with schistosomiasis based on positive Schistosoma serology and responded to praziquantel. Amoebiasis was evaluated and ruled out (E0 contradicted) -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Laboratory data, including carcinoembryonic antigen, carbohydrate antigen 19-9, interferon-gamma release assay (IGRA), purified protein derivative skin test, Entamoeba histolytica antibody, human immunodeficiency virus antibody, and fecal examinations, including culture and polymerase chain reaction for Mycobacterium tuberculosis, revealed no remarkable findings.

rationale: A 63-year-old male presenting with positive fecal occult blood test and colonic strictures. Serological testing for Entamoeba histolytica antibody was negative ('revealed no remarkable findings'). The patient was diagnosed with intestinal spirochetosis and subsequent mucinous carcinoma of the colon. Amoebiasis was evaluated and ruled out (E0 contradicted) -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: The serum findings of an evaluation for Entamoeba histolytica, cysticercus, Schistosoma sp., Toxocara, Echinococcus sp., Fasciola sp., Strongyloides stercoralis, Gnathostoma sp., Ancylostoma caninum, Toxoplasma gondii, Paragonimus sp., Trichinella spiralis, and Helicobacter pylori were normal, and the serum ELISA tests of E. histolytica, cysticercus, Schistosoma sp., Toxocara, Echinococcus sp., Fasciola sp., S. stercoralis, Gnathostoma sp., A. caninum, T. gondii, Paragonimus sp., T. spiralis, and H. pylori were negative.

rationale: A 12-year-old girl presenting with fever, headache, and CSF eosinophilic pleocytosis. Serum ELISA for Entamoeba histolytica was explicitly negative. Angiostrongyliasis was definitively confirmed via positive serum and CSF ELISA/Western blot against Angiostrongylus cantonensis. Amoebiasis was evaluated and excluded -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: We performed serological enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) tests for Entamoeba histolytica, Strongyloides, Toxocara, and Echinococcus and examined stool for the eggs of Fasciola hepatica. All results were negative.

rationale: A 50-year-old female presenting with RUQ pain and large cystic lesions in the liver and left ventricle. Serological ELISA for Entamoeba histolytica was explicitly negative ('All results were negative'). Histopathology of resected tissue confirmed cardiac and hepatic echinococcosis. Amoebiasis was evaluated and excluded -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: negative serology to hydatid, amebiasis, hepatitis B virus (HBV), hepatitis C virus (HCV), syphilis and toxoplasmosis, while serology to CMV IgG was positive but negative to IgM, COVID-19 RT-PCR and IgG antibodies raised to SARS-CoV-2 were negative, and the patient also presented with negative sputum evaluated by the Xpert MTB/RIF (Genexpert  Cepheid Inc, California, USA) and three Acid-Fast Bacilli (AFB) smear microscopy, three cultures of stool and parasitological stool examination were also negative, in addition to a blood culture.
A wet smear was negative for Entamoeba histolytica trophozoite.

rationale: A 26-year-old female PLWHA with multiple liver abscesses and melena. Serology for amebiasis was negative, and a wet smear of the abscess pus was negative for Entamoeba histolytica trophozoites. Pus culture confirmed Salmonella enterica subsp enterica pyogenic liver abscess, prompting cessation of metronidazole. Amoebiasis was evaluated and definitively ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Antibodies to Entamoeba histolytica and Echinococcus were checked and were negative.

rationale: A 5-year-old male presenting with a multicystic liver mass. Serologic antibodies to Entamoeba histolytica were tested and were explicitly negative. Histopathologic examination of the resected hepatic mass confirmed a mesenchymal hamartoma. Amoebic liver abscess was evaluated and excluded -> NEGATIVE.

step3_patient_anchor.coreference_notes: Second patient described in the report

evidence_items.source_quote: Multiple stool samples were also negative for ova and parasites such as Enterobius vermicularis, Entamoeba histolytica, Cryptosporidium, and Giardia species.

Actually, a serological work-up for zoonosis (Brucella, Coxiella, Rickettsia, Borrelia, Leptospira, Leishmania, and other parasites including investigation for Trichinella, Entamoeba, and Echinococcus), sexually transmitted diseases (syphilis, N. gonorrhoeae, U. urealyticum, M. hominis, and C. trachomatis), viral hepatitis A, B, C, and E, and human immunodeficiency virus tested negative.

rationale: An 18-year-old male presenting with fever, arthritis, and third-degree atrioventricular block diagnosed with acute rheumatic fever. Stool parasitological examinations and serology for Entamoeba were repeatedly negative. Amoebiasis was evaluated in the differential workup and excluded -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: His results for brucellosis, HIV, leishmaniasis, amebiasis, echinococcosis, and cytomegalovirus serology were all negative; furthermore, a rectal snip biopsy was negative for ova, and no schistosomal ova were detected in the patient's urine or stool.

rationale: A 29-year-old male presenting with bilateral lower extremity weakness and urinary incontinence diagnosed with spinal neuroschistosomiasis. Serological testing for amebiasis was explicitly negative. Amebiasis was evaluated in the differential infectious workup and ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Amoebic serology was negative.
Wet-mount examination showed no trophozoites of Entamoeba histolytica or any fungal element.

rationale: A 45-year-old male with poorly controlled diabetes presenting with a large hepatic abscess. Percutaneous drainage and culture confirmed a pyogenic liver abscess caused by Streptococcus pneumoniae. Amoebic serology was negative and wet-mount microscopy of the drained pus showed no trophozoites of Entamoeba histolytica. Amoebiasis was evaluated in the differential and definitively ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Nucleic acid amplification-based testing of a stool specimen was negative for adenovirus, Campylobacter, Cyclospora cayetanensis, Clostridium difficile, enteroaggregative Escherichia coli, enteropathogenic E. coli, enterotoxigenic E. coli, Shiga-like toxin producing E. coli, Shigella, enteroinvasive E. coli, Entamoeba histolytica, Giardia lamblia, human astrovirus, norovirus GI/GII, Plesiomonas shigelloides, rotavirus A, Salmonella, sapovirus, Vibrio, Vibrio cholera, and Yersinia enterocolitica (FilmArray  Gastrointestinal Panel, BioFire Diagnostics LLC, Salt Lake City, UT).

rationale: A 50-year-old female returning traveler presenting with fever, diarrhea, and syncope confirmed with Plasmodium falciparum malaria and non-typhoidal Salmonella bacteremia. Stool nucleic acid amplification testing (BioFire FilmArray GI Panel) was negative for Entamoeba histolytica. Amoebiasis was evaluated as an infectious etiology for diarrhea and ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Infectious studies of stool and blood including influenza A and B, parainfluenza, adenovirus, Epstein-Barr virus, amebiasis, Cryptosporidium parvum, cytomegalovirus, Clostridium difficile, Salmonella, Campylobacter, Yersinia, and Shigella were all found negative.

rationale: A 4-year-old female following autologous stem cell transplantation for stage 4 neuroblastoma presenting with severe enterocolitis and secretory diarrhea. Comprehensive infectious workup of stool and blood including amebiasis was entirely negative. Endoscopy and histopathological biopsies confirmed gastrointestinal graft-versus-host disease (GVHD). Amoebiasis was evaluated in the differential and ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: In addition, AFP < 2.0 ng/mL and Entamoeba histolytica IgG was negative.

rationale: A 65-year-old male presenting with a 13 cm multiseptated hepatic abscess following dental cleaning. Serologic testing for Entamoeba histolytica IgG was negative, while blood and abscess fluid cultures isolated Streptococcus intermedius, confirming pyogenic liver abscess. Amoebiasis was evaluated and definitively ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Serologic test for Hepatitis B virus (HBV), hepatitis C virus (HCV), Cytomegalovirus (CMV), HIV, Toxoplasmosis, Entamoeba histolytica, Leishmania brazilensis, donovani, and EBV IgM were all negative.

rationale: A 17-year-old female presenting with left upper quadrant pain and a 15 cm splenic cyst. Infectious and parasitic serologies including Entamoeba histolytica and Echinococcus were negative. Surgical exploration with cyst un-roofing and pathology confirmed a benign splenic epithelial cyst. Amoebiasis was evaluated in the differential and ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Moreover, the gastrointestinal PCR panel test for common pathogens was also negative. This panel test targets bacterial infections (Campylobacter jejuni, Campylobacter coli, C. difficile toxin A/B, Salmonella spp, Vibrio cholerae, Yersinia enterocolitica, Enteroaggregative E. coli, Enteropathogenic E. coli, Enterotoxigenic E. coli, Shigella-like toxin-producing E. coli, Shigella spp), parasitic infections (Cryptosporidium, Entamoeba histolytica, Giardia lamblia) and viral infections (Adenovirus, Astrovirus, Norovirus, Rotavirus A, Sapovirus).

rationale: A 74-year-old male presenting with bloody diarrhea and fever following SARS-CoV-2 infection. Stool gastrointestinal PCR multiplex panel targeting Entamoeba histolytica and other enteric pathogens was negative. Ileocolonoscopy and mucosal biopsies demonstrated cryptitis and crypt architectural distortion confirming ulcerative colitis. Amoebiasis was evaluated and ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: However blood cultures and antibodies for Echinococcus and Entamoeba histolytica were negative.

rationale: A 30-year-old male presenting with fever and a 7 cm hepatic mass mimicking liver abscess or neoplasm. Serological antibodies for Entamoeba histolytica and Echinococcus were negative, and tissue cultures were sterile. Liver resection and histopathology confirmed a solitary necrotic nodule secondary to portal vein thrombosis. Amoebiasis was evaluated and ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Stool cultures for Salmonella, Shigella, Campylobacter, Clostridium difficile, Giardia sp., Cryptosporidium sp., Entamoeba histolytica, and fecal antigens for rotavirus and adenovirus were negative.

rationale: A 22-month-old male presenting with chronic watery diarrhea, malnutrition, and abdominal distension diagnosed with celiac crisis. Infectious enteric evaluation including stool testing for Entamoeba histolytica, Giardia, Cryptosporidium, and bacterial pathogens was negative. Markedly elevated anti-TG2 IgA (>328 U/mL) and positive antiendomysial antibodies confirmed celiac disease. Amoebiasis was evaluated and ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Entamoeba histolytica Abs, echinococcus Abs, leismania Abs, brucella Abs were negative.

rationale: A 23-year-old previously healthy male presenting with high fever and right upper quadrant abdominal pain due to bilateral hepatic abscesses. Percutaneous drainage and culture confirmed Aggregatibacter aphrophilus pyogenic liver abscess. Entamoeba histolytica serology was tested and explicitly negative. With a confirmed pyogenic bacterial etiology and negative amebic serology, amoebiasis was ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: COVID-19 testing, interferon-gamma release assay, Entamoeba histolytica, and Echinococcus serologies were all negative.

rationale: A 71-year-old male with severe sepsis and altered mental status found to have a 6 x 4.6 cm rim-enhancing liver abscess. Serology for Entamoeba histolytica was explicitly negative. Abscess aspirate grew Gram-positive cocci and blood cultures speciated Brevibacterium, confirming pyogenic bacterial liver abscess responding to ampicillin-sulbactam. Amoebic etiology was ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: This rash was extensively evaluated in the past with negative PAS stain for fungus, immunofluorescence study, ANA test, anti-mitochondrial antibody, ANCA, celiac antibody test, stool for Entamoeba histolytica/other enteric pathogens (including cryptosporidium and giardiasis), strongyloides antibody serology, urinary Chlamydia and Neisseria gonorrhea testing.

rationale: A 30-year-old male with HIV presenting with extensive generalized erosive rash diagnosed by viral PCR as eczema herpeticum (HSV-1 and HSV-2). Prior extensive workup for recalcitrant dermatitis included stool examination for Entamoeba histolytica and other enteric pathogens, which was explicitly negative. Target disease excluded -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: the patient was initially diagnosed by the pediatric department with amoebiasis after a positive stool antigen test and was treated with oral 15 mg/kg metronidazole for 10 days and antimotility agents; however, his symptoms failed to resolve.
evidence_items.test_name: Initial stool antigen test and therapeutic trial of metronidazole

evidence_items.source_quote: The histopathology of the resected ileocecal segment was consistent with Burkitt lymphoma.

rationale: A 4-year-old male child presenting with severe colicky abdominal pain, intractable vomiting, and marked weight loss. He was initially diagnosed with amoebiasis based on a stool antigen test and treated with metronidazole for 10 days with complete lack of response. Subsequent imaging and laparotomy with ileocecal resection definitively confirmed ileocecal intussusception caused by stage II Burkitt lymphoma on histopathology and immunohistochemistry (CD20+, CD10+, C-MYC+). Amoebiasis was an initial misdiagnosis refuted by the confirmed neoplastic etiology and lack of therapeutic response -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Gastrointestinal PCR panel was negative for enterotoxigenic E. coli, Giardia, Norovirus, Salmonella, Shiga-like Toxin producing E. coli, Plesiomonas shigelloides, Vibrio, Yersinia enterocolitica, enteroaggregative E. coli, Cyclospora cayetanensis, Entamoeba histolytica, Adenovirus F 40/41, Astrovirus, Sapovirus, Enteropathogenic E. coli, and Shigella/Enteroinvasive E. coli.

rationale: A 40-year-old male post-liver transplant presenting with fever and watery diarrhea. Comprehensive multiplex gastrointestinal PCR panel was explicitly negative for Entamoeba histolytica. Peripheral blood PCR subsequently confirmed Ehrlichia chaffeensis (human monocytic ehrlichiosis) with prompt recovery upon doxycycline treatment. Target disease amoebiasis ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: The mycobacterial investigations for tuberculosis, amoebiasis, and Burkholderia pseudomallei, three important causes for liver abscess in South Asian region were negative.

rationale: A 68-year-old male presenting with RUQ abdominal pain found to have an 8.3 x 10.8 cm hepatic abscess. Percutaneous drainage aspirate grew Escherichia coli. Specific diagnostic investigations for amoebiasis were explicitly negative. Colonoscopy revealed an impacted denture causing sigmoid microperforation as the source of pyogenic liver abscess, resolving with cefotaxime. Amoebiasis ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Qualitative antibodies for toxoplasmosis, human immunodeficiency virus, and Entamoeba histolytica were negative.
evidence_items.test_name: Qualitative antibody testing for Entamoeba histolytica

rationale: A 36-year-old female presenting with recurrent RUQ abdominal pain and necrotizing granulomatous hepatic pseudotumor requiring partial hepatectomy. Diagnostic evaluation for infectious etiologies included qualitative antibody testing for Entamoeba histolytica, which was explicitly negative. Target disease excluded -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Laboratory testing was negative for hepatitis A IgM, hepatitis B core antibody IgM, hepatitis B surface antigen, hepatitis C antibody, HIV antibody 1 and 2, Entamoeba histolytica IgG, and Echinococcus IgG antibody.
A 16S PCR sent for next-generation sequencing from the aspirate returned positive for F. nucleatum.

rationale: A 51-year-old male veteran presenting with abdominal pain, distension, and multiseptated cystic hepatic masses. Diagnostic workup for hepatic abscess etiologies included Entamoeba histolytica IgG serology, which was explicitly negative. Abscess aspirate 16S PCR identified Fusobacterium nucleatum. Amoebiasis was evaluated as part of the differential workup for liver lesions and ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: A thorough laboratory work-up was initiated and resulted in negative results for antinuclear antibody (ANA), rheumatoid factor (RF), antineutrophilic cytoplasmic antibody (ANCA), anticyclic citrullinated peptide (CCP) antibodies, coccidioides serum antibody, human immunodeficiency virus (HIV), syphilis immunoglobulin M (IgM), syphilis immunoglobulin G (IgG), sputum acid fast bacilli (AFB) stain, stool ova and parasite stain, Cryptococcus neoformans antigen, Toxocara IgG, Entamoeba histolytica IgG, serum beta-D-glucan, fungal pleural fluid culture, and pleural fluid KOH smear.
evidence_items.test_name: Entamoeba histolytica IgG and stool O&P

rationale: A 45-year-old male presenting with abdominal distension, diarrhea, and eosinophilic ascites/pleural effusion. Diagnostic workup to rule out infectious causes of hypereosinophilia included stool ova and parasite exam and Entamoeba histolytica IgG, which were both negative. Amoebiasis was evaluated and ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: A gastrointestinal multiplex PCR panel (Campylobacter (C. jejuni/C. coli/C. upsaliensis), Clostridioides (Clostridium) difficile (toxin A/B), Plesiomonas shigelloides, Salmonella, Yersinia enterocolitica, Vibrio (V. parahaemolyticus/V. vulnificus/V. cholerae), Vibrio cholerae, Enteroaggregative E. coli, Enteropathogenic E. coli, Enterotoxigenic E. coli lt/st, Shiga-like toxin-producing E. coli stx1/stx2, E. coli O157, Shigella/Enteroinvasive E. coli; Cryptosporidium, Cyclospora cayetanensis, Entamoeba histolytica, Giardia lamblia; Adenovirus F40/41, Astrovirus, Norovirus GI/GII, Rotavirus A, Sapovirus (I, II, IV, and V) also revealed Clostridium difficile (toxin A/B)

rationale: A 38-year-old female with agammaglobulinemia presenting with chronic diarrhea. A comprehensive stool gastrointestinal multiplex PCR panel covering multiple enteropathogens including Entamoeba histolytica was performed; Entamoeba histolytica was negative (panel only revealed C. difficile). Amoebiasis was evaluated and ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: We sent an Entamoeba histolytica immunoglobulin G (IgG) enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA) and a hepatic abscess pus aspiration for C/S to rule out other common causes of liver abscesses, such as an amoebic liver abscess or a pyogenic liver abscess. Both tests came back negative (Table 3).
The CBNAAT of both specimens showed the presence of Mycobacterium tuberculosis (MTB), which was sensitive to rifampicin.
evidence_items.specimen: liver abscess pus and lymph node

rationale: A 46-year-old female presenting with fever, RUQ pain, and a solitary liquefied liver abscess. Entamoeba histolytica IgG ELISA was tested to rule out amoebic liver abscess and was explicitly negative. Cartridge-based nucleic acid amplification testing (CBNAAT) of abscess pus confirmed Mycobacterium tuberculosis. Amoebiasis was evaluated in the differential and ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Serology for entamoeba histolytica and echinococcus granulosus antibodies was negative.
Diagnosis: a ruptured gas-forming pyogenic liver abscess was diagnosed, and a differential diagnosis of perforated viscus was made.

rationale: A 39-year-old male diabetic presenting with peritonitis secondary to a ruptured gas-forming hepatic abscess requiring exploratory laparotomy. Diagnostic evaluation included serology for Entamoeba histolytica, which was explicitly negative. Patient was diagnosed with a pyogenic liver abscess. Amoebiasis was evaluated and ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Stool routine and microscopic investigations showed no cyst or ova; amoebic serology of the blood was negative.
Polymerase chain reaction (PCR) analysis of gastric secretions for detection of Mycobacterium tuberculosis was positive.

rationale: An 8-year-old female presenting with fever, abdominal pain, and a ruptured liver abscess. Stool microscopy was negative for cysts or ova, and amoebic blood serology was explicitly negative. Gastric aspirate PCR confirmed Mycobacterium tuberculosis, establishing a diagnosis of tuberculous liver abscess. Amoebiasis was evaluated in the differential and ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: After ruling out the infectious causes, such as amebiasis infection, clostridium difficile, and HIV, and based on this evidence, Crohn's disease was managed as a highly suspicious diagnosis.

rationale: A 27-year-old male presenting with severe abdominal pain, duodenal stricture, and focal active colitis. Infectious etiologies of colitis including amebiasis infection were explicitly evaluated and ruled out ('After ruling out the infectious causes, such as amebiasis infection, clostridium difficile, and HIV...'). The patient was subsequently diagnosed with chronic granulomatous disease. Amoebiasis was evaluated and ruled out -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Due to previously mentioned signs of colitis in MRI, a feces analysis was performed and revealed no evidence of infectious diarrhea, including amebiasis.
evidence_items.test_name: Feces analysis for infectious diarrhea including amebiasis

rationale: A 33-year-old male with subphrenic, retrosplenic, and hepatic abscesses extending transdiaphragmatically to cause purulent pericarditis and cardiac tamponade. Feces analysis performed to evaluate colitis showed no evidence of infectious diarrhea, including amebiasis. Purulent drainage fluid grew Bacteroides fragilis, Hungatella hathewayi, and Fusobacterium nucleatum, confirming pyogenic bacterial infection. Amoebiasis was evaluated and ruled out (E0) -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: An extensive infectious and inflammatory evaluation, including stool cultures, ova and parasite examination, celiac serologies, tuberculosis testing, and serologic testing for Entamoeba histolytica, was unrevealing.
evidence_items.test_name: Serologic testing for Entamoeba histolytica and stool O&P

rationale: A 39-year-old female presenting with chronic cramping abdominal pain, diarrhea, and colonic strictures. Comprehensive infectious evaluation including serologic testing for Entamoeba histolytica and stool ova and parasite examination was unrevealing (negative). Resection histopathology revealed diffuse infiltration by signet-ring cells diagnostic of metastatic gastric adenocarcinoma. Amoebiasis was evaluated and ruled out (E0) -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Enteric Parasites Panel (Giardia lamblia, Entamoeba histolytica, Cryptosporidium spp.).
evidence_items.test_name: BD MAX Enteric Parasites multiplex PCR panel

evidence_items.source_quote: The PCR result was positive for Salmonella; all other targets tested negative.
evidence_items.test_name: Multiplex PCR panel result (all other targets tested negative)

rationale: A 41-year-old patient presenting with acute watery diarrhea and fever. Multiplex PCR testing on the BD MAX Enteric Parasites Panel specifically targeting Entamoeba histolytica (along with Giardia lamblia and Cryptosporidium) was negative. Diagnostic evaluation confirmed a novel Salmonella enterica serovar (Salmonella Weitmar). Amoebiasis was explicitly tested and ruled out (E0) -> NEGATIVE.

evidence_items.source_quote: Following this, quantitative polymerase chain reaction (qPCR) was performed to target Giardia intestinalis, Entamoeba histolytica, Cryptosporidium spp., and Dientamoeba fragilis as previously published.
evidence_items.test_name: Quantitative real-time PCR targeting Entamoeba histolytica

evidence_items.source_quote: The qPCR analysis revealed the presence of B. hominis DNA, with a Ct value of 40.29 (Figure 2).

rationale: A 20-year-old male with newly diagnosed HIV presenting with bloody, mucoid diarrhea. Multiplex quantitative PCR (qPCR) specifically targeting Entamoeba histolytica, Giardia intestinalis, and Cryptosporidium spp. was negative, while microscopy and specific qPCR established Blastocystis hominis infection. Gastrointestinal amoebiasis was specifically tested and excluded (E0) -> NEGATIVE.
